summary.text: A 10-year-old castrated male Maltese weighing 2.0 kg was referred for acute non-weight-bearing right hind limb lameness. History included bilateral tibial tuberosity transposition one year earlier for medial patellar luxation, stage B2 myxomatous mitral valve disease, and pimobendan, furosemide and enalapril.

Examination showed a positive cranial drawer motion of the right stifle, and radiographs confirmed cranial displacement of the tibia with mild periarticular osteophyte formation, consistent with cranial cruciate ligament rupture. Prior TTT changes were noted, and pre-anesthetic screening revealed no contraindications to anesthesia.

Under butorphanol and midazolam premedication, propofol induction and sevoflurane maintenance, with bupivacaine infiltration, a hybrid intra-articular and extracapsular stabilization was performed using 1.1-mm bone tunnels and a Ligafiba synthetic ligament with clamp, bypassing the lateral fabella. A Robert Jones bandage was applied for 7 days, followed by strict cage rest for about 4 weeks.

Controlled leash walking was introduced after 1 month. Recovery progressed uneventfully with no complications observed, and follow-up up to 7 months postoperatively showed the dog free of lameness or discomfort with stable limb function and no recurrence.
